title: How do we know the continents move?
new_ideas: device TornNews — a newspaper torn in two whose line of print runs on across the tear

lines.text: Every so often, Earth’s magnetic field flips. North becomes south. A compass would swing round and point the other *way*.

plan.see: A big compass on the desk: its needle swings round and points south, then back, again and again.
plan.beats: +0.0 the needle points north | +1.4 it swings | +2.6 south | +3.8 it swings back | +5.0 again | +7.2 the camera travels on toward the needle

becomes.to: a big compass on the desk: its needle swings round and points south, then back, again and again

acts: the camera travels on toward the needle

lines.text: At the ridge, hot melted rock wells up from below, cools, and locks in the direction of the field, like music recorded onto a *tape*.

plan.see: Cross-section of the ridge: glowing rock wells up, cools from orange to dark; tiny arrows inside freeze pointing north.
plan.beats: +0.0 a crack in the floor | +1.4 glowing rock wells up | +2.8 it cools | +4.2 arrows freeze inside | +5.4 a tape head icon | +7.6 the camera travels on toward the welling rock | +9.8 the light shifts across the welling rock

becomes.to: cross-section of the ridge: glowing rock wells up, cools from orange to dark; tiny arrows inside freeze pointing north

acts: the camera travels on toward the welling rock
the light shifts across the welling rock

lines.text: Then it’s pushed aside by newer rock, and newer, out to both sides. The sea floor is a tape recorder, playing out in two *directions*.

plan.see: The floor moves out both ways like two tapes from a reel; each band carries its arrows away.
plan.beats: +0.0 the floor shoves outward | +1.4 a new band forms | +2.8 another | +4.2 the bands march away | +5.6 reels turn at the edges | +7.8 the camera travels on toward the two tapes moving | +10.0 the light shifts across the two tapes moving

becomes.to: the floor moves out both ways like two tapes from a reel; each band carries its arrows away

acts: the camera travels on toward the two tapes moving
the light shifts across the two tapes moving
lines.motif: the seam — the ridge as a tape head

lines.text: So that is why the sea floor is striped: the stripes are the flips, written into stone. The ocean floor is being made right now, and it is *moving*.

plan.see: The arrows in each band flip N/S; the bands light gold and dark in alternation — the stripes.
plan.beats: +0.0 arrows north | +1.2 next band south | +2.4 north | +3.4 the bands become the stripes | +5.6 the light shifts across the alternating arrows | +7.8 the camera travels on toward the alternating arrows | +10.0 the light shifts across the alternating arrows

lines.reads: Stripes are the flips. The floor moves.

becomes.to: the arrows in each band flip N/S; the bands light gold and dark in alternation — the stripes

acts: the light shifts across the alternating arrows
the camera travels on toward the alternating arrows
the light shifts across the alternating arrows

lines.text: If the sea floor moves, the continents ride along with it. They don’t plough through the ocean; they travel with it, like boxes on a conveyor *belt*.

plan.see: The floor becomes a conveyor belt; continents sit on it like parcels and ride away; it passes a snowy grave.
plan.beats: +0.0 the belt runs | +1.4 Africa rides on it | +2.8 South America the other way | +4.2 a snowy cross rides past | +5.6 the cross is gently carried | +7.8 the camera travels on toward the parcels riding | +10.0 the light shifts across the parcels riding

lines.reads: The continents ride the moving floor.

becomes.to: the floor becomes a conveyor belt; continents sit on it like parcels and ride away; it passes a snowy grave

acts: the camera travels on toward the parcels riding
the light shifts across the parcels riding

lines.text: Wegener was right that the continents move. He was wrong only about how. The Earth’s outer shell is cracked into giant moving *plates*.

plan.see: A globe: its shell cracks like an eggshell into plates, outlined in vermilion.
plan.beats: +0.0 a globe | +1.4 the first crack | +2.6 cracks spread | +3.8 plates outlined | +5.0 they shift a little | +7.2 the camera travels on toward the cracking shell | +9.4 the light shifts across the cracking shell

becomes.to: a globe: its shell cracks like an eggshell into plates, outlined in vermilion

acts: the camera travels on toward the cracking shell
the light shifts across the cracking shell

lines.text: Where plates pull apart, new sea floor is born. Where they push together, one dives deep under the other, and the ground *shakes*.

plan.see: Cross-section: one plate slides down under another into the hot mantle; earthquake stars flash along the edge.
plan.beats: +0.0 two plates meet | +1.4 one bends down | +2.8 it slides under | +4.2 quakes flash | +5.4 a volcano puffs | +7.6 the camera travels on toward the diving plate

lines.reads: New floor at ridges; old floor dives at trenches.

becomes.to: cross-section: one plate slides down under another into the hot mantle; earthquake stars flash along the edge

acts: the camera travels on toward the diving plate

lines.text: Where two continents crash, the land crumples like a rug shoved against a wall. That is how the Himalaya were *born*.

plan.see: A rug slides along a floor into a wall and wrinkles; the wrinkles become snowy Himalayan peaks.
plan.beats: +0.0 a rug slides | +1.4 it hits a wall | +2.6 it wrinkles | +3.8 the wrinkles turn to peaks | +5.0 snow on the peaks | +7.2 the camera travels on toward the rug wrinkling

becomes.to: a rug slides along a floor into a wall and wrinkles; the wrinkles become snowy Himalayan peaks

acts: the camera travels on toward the rug wrinkling

lines.text: And the Atlantic, where Wegener first saw the tear, is still opening today, along the seam where South America and Africa came *apart*.

plan.see: From above: the Atlantic with the ridge running down its middle; the two sides creep apart.
plan.beats: +0.0 we rise above the ocean | +1.4 the ridge seam glows | +2.8 the coasts creep apart | +4.2 the seam widens a hair | +6.4 the light shifts across the ridge seam | +8.6 the camera travels on toward the ridge seam

becomes.to: from above: the Atlantic with the ridge running down its middle; the two sides creep apart

acts: the light shifts across the ridge seam
the camera travels on toward the ridge seam
lines.motif: the seam — the Atlantic tear today

lines.text: We can measure it now from space. Satellites send signals to markers bolted into rock on each *continent*, and time them precisely.

plan.see: A satellite above; beams drop to a brass marker bolted into rock; a tiny distance ticks up.
plan.beats: +0.0 a satellite glides | +1.4 a beam drops | +2.8 it hits a marker | +4.0 another beam | +5.2 numbers tick | +7.4 the camera travels on toward the beam on the marker

becomes.to: a satellite above; beams drop to a brass marker bolted into rock; a tiny distance ticks up

acts: the camera travels on toward the beam on the marker

lines.text: The answer: a few centimetres every year. About as fast as your fingernails *grow*.

plan.see: A ruler beside the marker, then a hand beside the ruler: the fingernail and the gap grow together.
plan.beats: +0.0 a ruler lays down | +1.4 a hand rests beside it | +2.6 the nail grows | +3.6 the gap grows the same

becomes.to: a ruler beside the marker, then a hand beside the ruler: the fingernail and the gap grow together

lines.text: Too slow to see. But give it two hundred million years, and that fingernail’s width became a whole *ocean*.

plan.see: The nail line becomes the Atlantic: Pangaea’s quilt seam opens out stitch by stitch into an ocean.
plan.beats: +0.0 the nail line glows | +1.4 it becomes the quilt seam | +2.8 the stitches pop | +4.2 the ocean opens | +5.4 a counter: 200 million years | +7.6 the camera travels on toward the opening seam

acts: the camera travels on toward the opening seam
lines.motif: the seam — the quilt opens into the Atlantic

lines.text: And it hasn’t stopped. Far in the future the continents will fit together again in a new way, a puzzle no one has ever *seen*.

plan.see: Time runs forward: continents drift into a new arrangement and become pieces of a jigsaw on the child’s table.
plan.beats: +0.0 continents drift | +1.4 they cross | +2.8 a new shape forms | +4.2 it becomes jigsaw pieces | +5.4 on the table again | +7.6 the camera travels on toward the new puzzle | +9.8 the light shifts across the new puzzle

becomes.to: time runs forward: continents drift into a new arrangement and become pieces of a jigsaw on the child’s table

acts: the camera travels on toward the new puzzle
the light shifts across the new puzzle

lines.text: Alfred Wegener never saw the proof. But the torn edges he noticed in an old atlas were real. The world really had been pulled *apart*.

plan.see: Beside the jigsaw, the old torn atlas from the start; his photograph slides into the tear.
plan.beats: +0.0 the torn atlas lies there | +1.4 a photo slides in | +2.8 the lamp warms | +4.2 the halves inch apart | +6.4 the light shifts across the torn atlas | +8.6 the camera travels on toward the torn atlas

acts: the light shifts across the torn atlas
the camera travels on toward the torn atlas
lines.motif: the seam — the torn atlas again

lines.text: The ground under your feet is moving right now. Slowly, quietly, about as fast as your fingernails grow… and it always *has*.
